content:
The test image shows a very young soybean seedling that has completely collapsed at/near the soil line on sandy soil, exhibiting a shepherd's crook bend and lying wilted/dead. Healthy seedlings are visible nearby. This is classic early-season damping off.

Key observations:
- Young seedling completely collapsed/dead at soil line
- Sandy soil environment
- Shepherd's crook stem bend
- Surrounding plants healthy

The Pythium reference confirms this pattern — seedlings rotting/collapsing at hypocotyl level with soft rot, leading to complete plant death in early emergence. This matches Pythium damping off description: "water-soaked lesions on hypocotyl or cotyledons developing into brown soft rot; diseased plants are easily pulled from soil due to rotted roots."
